subject: Special damages carve-out — mutuality options for MSA (Acme)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Special damages carve-out — proposal and next steps

Tom — following up from our call this morning. Acme legal flagged the special/incidental/punitive damages carve-out and asked for clarity on two points: whether Redwood's exclusion should be mutual, and how we define "consequential / special / incidental" for the MSA.

Quick context: Redwood's standard MSA excludes consequential, special, incidental, punitive damages one-way (customer keeps statutory remedies and Redwood keeps commercial liability capped). Acme is pushing for mutual language and also wants a non-exhaustive definition tied to foreseeability and upstream third-party claims.

Attached: ACME_MSA_redlines_v1.docx (includes our suggested mutual compromise in §9) and redline_summary_table.xlsx with line items.

Suggested next steps:
- Acme to confirm whether mutual exclusion is a hard requirement for procurement.
- If mutuality is non-negotiable, ask Acme to adopt Redwood's definition of consequential (limited to loss of profits, loss of data, business interruption) and keep a separate carve-in for breach of confidentiality/indemnity where caps don't apply.

Can you confirm procurement's stance or loop in their counsel? I can draft a concise compromise paragraph for sign-off.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Special damages carve-out — proposal and next steps

Jasmine — appreciate the quick follow. Short answers: procurement really wants mutuality; legal is worried about leaving open a path for Redwood to claim massive consequential losses in a downstream vendor failure scenario. They also asked for a clearer definition so they aren't surprised later.

I'm copying our lead counsel, Sarah Mills (legal@acme.com), who will propose exact wording. In the meantime, two asks from procurement:
1) If mutuality is required, can Redwood accept mutual exclusion but preserve an express exception for gross negligence and willful misconduct?
2) Can we get specific examples in the definition (e.g., lost profits, business interruption, loss of goodwill) but add "not limited to" language?

Happy to take your compromise language and run it past Sarah.

—Tom
Tom Keller
Director, Strategic Procurement | Acme Corporation

From: Sarah Mills <legal@acme.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Tom Keller <tkeller@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Special damages carve-out — proposal and next steps

Jasmine — thanks for sharing. Draft issues from legal:
- Mutual exclusion is acceptable only if both parties' direct damages remain uncapped or caps are aligned. Acme cannot accept a situation where Redwood retains a full $X cap while Acme has statutory remedies uncapped.
- We want the definition of "consequential" to point to foreseeability and a non-exhaustive list. However, Acme insists on a carve-in: losses arising from Redwood's failure to comply with data protection obligations or intentional breach of confidentiality are outside the exclusion and subject to uncapped damages.

Proposed wording suggestion (high-level):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages, except to the extent such damages arise from: (a) each party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) a breach of the Confidentiality or Data Protection obligations; or (c) a party's indemnification obligations to third parties for infringement claims."

If Redwood is able to propose language that aligns caps symmetrically (or explains why caps differ), legal will be more open to mutuality.

Regards,
Sarah Mills
Senior Counsel | Acme Corporation
legal@acme.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Mills <legal@acme.com>, Tom Keller <tkeller@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Special damages carve-out — proposal and next steps

Team — looping in our legal POV. High-level position: Redwood can accept mutual exclusion subject to (1) symmetric caps tied to order form level (we'd prefer a per-order cap = greater of $1M or 3x fees paid in prior 12 months); and (2) explicit carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and breaches of confidentiality/data protection.

Suggested compromise paragraph to propose to Acme (drafted for clarity):
"Except for liability arising from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, a party's obligations under Section X (Confidentiality and Data Protection), or a party's indemnification obligations, neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, indirect or punitive damages, including loss of profits, loss of data, business interruption, or loss of goodwill. Notwithstanding the foregoing, each party's aggregate liability for direct damages arising under this Agreement shall be limited to the greater of $1,000,000 (one million dollars) or three times the fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form during the prior twelve (12) month period."

This preserves mutuality while protecting Redwood's predictable unit economics. If procurement at Acme insists on uncapped categories beyond confidentiality/data protection, we'll need exec approval.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Sarah / Tom — thanks for the clear ask and for drafting the high-level carve-in language. Attached is a short redline that implements Neha's compromise paragraph and aligns caps to Order Form amounts (see line 12–18).

Key points for Acme:
- Mutual exclusion with explicit carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, Confidentiality/Data Protection breaches, and indemnity obligations.
- Symmetric cap: greater of $1M or 3x prior 12 months fees (Order Form tie) — this prevents one-way exposure while keeping our commercial limits predictable.
- Definition list for "consequential" includes examples but will remain non-exhaustive; foreseeability will be referenced to limit surprise.

If this is acceptable to legal, we can update the Order Form and route to procurement for signature. Otherwise, please flag specific line items to escalate.

Best,
